documented_probe: The reference floors for the primer-design (hard), causal-adjustment (hard) and jaxley-biophysics (hard) competencies are intentionally exercised in a compact, self-contained form: a single small primer parts table (3-4 parts) with known flanks, a hand-sized causal DAG (<=6 nodes) with a declared effect and optional forbid list, and one small SWC morphology + params JSON ported into three jaxley channel classes. Each is real (correct primer overhang/anneal/Tm bounds, genuine minimal back-door adjustment sets, genuine ODE kinetics), so the competencies are honestly exercised, but the data scale keeps the overall task at the medium bucket rather than hard. Nothing is dropped or faked.
notes: Five slice competencies bundled into one /app/analyze.py whose public API is re-run on hidden inputs per competency: a size-configurable normalized 2D histogram with inclusive max edges; a ';'-delimited/','-decimal spectrum parser returning clean x/y; all inclusion-minimal back-door adjustment sets for a named effect (d-separation + descendants/forbid exclusions); golden-gate primer design with Wallace Tm and exact reference TSV serialization; and a NEURON MOD -> jaxley channel port driven to a voltage trace compared to a reference within tolerance. Difficulty comes from reasoning_depth (causal/back-door + Tm selection), dependent_stages (program authors + runs + verifier re-runs functions on visible and hidden inputs), hidden_case_generalization (all five have fresh hidden fixtures), tool_breadth (numpy, networkx/d-separation, jaxley), quantitative_correctness (exact TSV/JSON and trace tolerance). Rubric total 13 -> medium (10-17).
